defects.description: The required Introduction section is missing; the document goes straight from the Abstract to '1 Problem Statement' (p.1–2).
No dedicated Motivation section exists; motivation appears only as a 'Motivation/Objective' label in the Abstract (p.1).
No Objective section exists; Section 4 is 'System Requirements and Top Level Design' and Section 5 'Expected Findings' (p.3–4).
There are no per-objective subsections of at least two paragraphs each (Expected Findings, p.4).
The objectives in the Abstract (p.1) use passive or impersonal phrasing with several actions instead of single-verb action form.
The AI Transparency Statement is missing from the document.
The bibliography (p.5–6) lists only five publications, below the required 6–8.
The proposal contains only one figure (Figure 1, p.4); at least two are required.
Figure 1 (p.4) is a sequence diagram or otherwise not a suitable UML diagram, so the proposal has no suitable UML diagram.
Figure 1 is never referenced by number in the text; the only cross-reference is 'illustrated in section 4' (p.2).
The caption of Figure 1 (p.4) is short and generic rather than long and informative.
The Figure 1 caption (p.4) is in sentence case rather than title case.
The message labels inside Figure 1 (1.1–3.3, p.4) are treated as headings and are not in title case.
The title line 'with Artemis & GitLab CI' (p.1) is claimed not to be in title case.
The scenario labels 'Exercise work fow', 'Participating actors' and 'Flow of events' in Section 4 (p.3) are not in title case.
The task labels in the Time Schedule (p.5) are not in title case.
'Workflow' is spelled inconsistently ('workfow', 'work fow') in Section 4 and the Figure 1 caption (p.3–4).
An Abstract sentence starts with 'Since some Version Control (VC) systems...' (p.1).
A Problem Statement sentence starts with 'To achieve this goal...' (p.2).
A Related Work sentence starts with 'In order to implement this idea...' (p.2).
A Related Work sentence starts with 'Since the benefits of using CI...' (p.3).
A Proposed Solution sentence starts with 'As a result...' (p.2).
An Expected Findings sentence starts with 'As described in section 3...' (p.4).
A Related Work sentence is claimed to start with 'Since CI services are now often included...' (p.3).
A sentence is claimed to start with 'Because the build plan is fetched...' (p.3).
The abbreviation 'API' is never defined; it is first used in the Abstract (p.1) and again later.
The Abstract problem-statement passage uses the filler word 'Furthermore' (p.1).
The Problem Statement paragraph on Bamboo/Jenkins uses the filler 'additional server overhead' (p.2).
The Problem Statement paragraph on build-plan copying uses the fillers 'Additionally' and 'Especially' (p.2).
The Proposed Solution paragraph uses the fillers 'Furthermore' and 'additional effort' (p.2).
The Related Work paragraph on CI being included in VC servers uses the filler 'additional work' (p.3).
The Related Work paragraph on Hilton et al. uses the filler 'also' (p.3).
The Expected Findings paragraph 'In addition, universities will save time and money...' uses the filler 'In addition' (p.4).
The Expected Findings passage 'In addition, either Ansible or a Kubernetes cluster...' uses the filler 'In addition' (p.4).
The Problem Statement exam paragraph uses the intensifier 'very cumbersome' (p.2).
The Abstract problem-statement passage uses passive voice ('should be migrated', 'has been assigned') (p.1).
The Abstract proposed-solution passage uses the passive 'the build plan is fetched from the API' (p.1).
The Problem Statement build-plan paragraph uses passive voice ('is copied', 'are not patched', 'must be updated manually') (p.2).
The first Proposed Solution paragraph uses passive voice ('the build plan is fetched', 'could be transposed') (p.2).
The second Proposed Solution paragraph uses 'can be made available' and the awkward 'GitLab CI is downloading' (p.2).
The first Related Work paragraph uses the passive 'is build and tested' (p.2).
The Related Work Krusche paragraph uses passive voice ('is split up', 'was built', 'feedback generated') (p.2–3).
The Related Work sentence 'CI services are now often included with VC servers' uses passive voice (p.3).
The Related Work sentence 'it is useful to teach the concepts of CI' uses an impersonal construction (p.3).
The visionary-scenario steps in Section 4 use passive voice ('is copied', 'gets configured', 'gets triggered') (p.3).
The first Expected Findings paragraph uses the passive 'the API of Artemis might be extended' (p.4).
The last Expected Findings paragraph uses 'can be used' and 'it will be possible to tackle' (p.4).
The Time Schedule uses the passive 'It is planned to adhere to the following time schedule' (p.4).
The Time Schedule assumptions use the first-person 'I' (p.4).
The problem-statement passage in the Abstract (p.1) states solutions ('The CI server should be migrated...', 'it should be possible to adjust the build plan').
The exam paragraph of the Problem Statement (p.2) prescribes desired functionality: changing build plans, hiding tests and using a debug compiler.
The Problem Statement (p.2) does not explicitly identify the affected actors (instructors, students, administrators) or the negative impact on each.
The motivation text in the Abstract (p.1) is an implementation rationale that repeats the problem rather than a visionary motivation.
The Problem section (p.2) is claimed to exceed the 3/4-page limit.
The total proposal text (about 3.5 pages) is claimed to fall below the 4–6 page range.
The 'Motivation/Objective' paragraph of the Abstract is only 1–2 lines long (p.1).
The 'Problem Statement' paragraph of the Abstract is too short (p.1).
The 'Proposed Solution' paragraph of the Abstract is too short (p.1).
The '(Expected) Results' paragraph of the Abstract is too short (p.1).
The Abstract (p.1) is written as labelled list items instead of continuous prose.
The Abstract problem-statement passage (p.1) mixes two ideas: migrating the CI server and adjusting build plans.
The Bamboo/Jenkins paragraph of the Problem Statement is too short (p.2).
The build-plan copying paragraph of the Problem Statement is too short (p.2).
The exam paragraph of the Problem Statement is too short (p.2).
The first Related Work paragraph (p.2) mixes Booch, Fowler and Krusche et al.
The Krusche et al. paragraph in Related Work (p.2–3) is too long and covers several ideas.
The introductory sentence of Section 4, 'The visionary scenario presents...', is a one-line paragraph (p.3).
The closing sentence of Section 4, 'Using the problem statement section 1...', is a 1–2 line paragraph (p.3).
Section 4 (p.3) relies on a 14-step numbered workflow list instead of prose.
The Expected Findings paragraph 'On long term, we expect...' is too short (p.4).
The Expected Findings paragraph 'In addition, universities will save time and money...' is a 1–2 line paragraph (p.4).
The Expected Findings paragraph 'The proposed solution opens up new opportunities...' is too short (p.4).
The Ansible/Kubernetes passage in Expected Findings is too short (p.4).
The last Expected Findings paragraph (p.4) mixes unrelated ideas: further research, the exam problem and Ansible/Kubernetes deployment.
The numbered labels in Figure 1 (p.4) are treated as subsections and have no introductory text.
The CI component is called 'CI server', 'CI service', 'CI system' and 'CI application' interchangeably (p.1–3).
The Abstract says 'task' (p.1) while the rest of the document says 'exercise'.
'CI Server' (Problem Statement, p.2) is capitalized inconsistently with 'CI server' elsewhere.
'VC Server', 'VC server' and 'Version Control server' are used inconsistently (Proposed Solution, p.2).
The Time Schedule (p.4–5) is organized as single-week calendar items rather than 2–4 week iterations.
The Time Schedule (p.4–5) follows a waterfall timeline that is not agile and not tied to the objectives.
The prototype work in the Time Schedule (April–June, p.5) is split into horizontal layers rather than vertically integrated features.
The June schedule items 'Models' and 'Requirements' (p.5) are not measurable deliverables.
The September schedule item 'Revise models with concrete implementation' (p.5) is not a measurable deliverable.
The October schedule item 'Writing . . .' (p.5) is not a measurable deliverable.
The November schedule item 'Implement improvements' (p.5) is not a measurable deliverable.
The December schedule item 'Thesis' (p.5) is not a measurable deliverable.
The June schedule contains a dedicated 'Requirements' task (p.5).
The September schedule contains a documentation-writing task (p.5).
The October schedule entry is thesis writing ('Writing . . .', p.5).
The November schedule contains thesis review tasks ('Thesis ready for review', 'Review finished', p.5).
The December schedule entry is thesis completion ('1st week: Thesis', p.5).
The March schedule entry is proposal writing ('5th week: Proposal', p.5).
The schedule assumption 'Every week, Wednesday is set aside for working on the thesis' (p.4) is claimed to be a thesis-writing task.
The May schedule entry contains the typo '3nd week' (p.5).
In Expected Findings, a lowercase 'with' follows a full stop ('research. with', p.4).
Related Work contains the grammar error 'is build and tested' (p.2).
Related Work contains the grammar error 'an newly developed' (p.2).
Related Work duplicates a word in 'should take generally take place' (p.2).
